title: Know your address
briefing: New box: net-01. Before anything else, an operator needs to know how the
machine is wired — starting with its own IP address.
Interfaces and addresses come from the `ip` command.
tips: `ip addr` (or `ip a`) lists every interface. 'lo' is loopback; the real one is 'eth0'.
The address is the number after 'inet', before the /24.
objective: Find net-01's IPv4 address on eth0 and save just the address (no /24) to ~/ip.txt.
hints: List addresses: `ip addr show eth0`. Look at the 'inet' line.
The address is 10.10.0.7 (the part before /24). Write it to the file.
explanation: `ip addr` is the modern way to read a host's network config (the old `ifconfig` is deprecated). Every interface has a name and, usually, an 'inet' address with a /prefix — that /24 means the first 24 bits are the network, the rest is this host.
